title: A misclassified covariate that is both balanced and a modifier
question: When a binary effect modifier is misclassified in the source, the target or both, which corrections does population adjustment need, and is correcting the outcome model alone enough?
design: Anchored transport with a misclassified binary modifier under four assay scenarios and two modification strengths; naive, prevalence-corrected and latent-weight MAIC; naive, outcome-only corrected and fully corrected latent-class STC. 8 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: No. MAIC on a misclassified binary modifier was biased even with identical assays in both studies (-0.03 to -0.13 on the log odds ratio scale), because reweighting recorded categories leaves each category's true composition at the source's; correcting the target prevalence alone did not help. Correcting only STC's outcome model left bias of -0.012 to -0.051. Fully corrected STC and MAIC with weights chosen on the latent prevalence were unbiased (within 0.006).
findings: Refuting sentence fails: outcome-only correction biased beyond 3 MCSE and 0.03 in some scenarios (to -0.051).
MAIC on the recorded covariate with identical assays: bias beyond 3 MCSE in 4 of 4 scenarios.
Latent-prevalence MAIC and fully corrected STC: bias -0.006 to 0.006.
not_answered: Known assay parameters; one binary covariate; no interval assessment. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Marginal log odds ratio, A versus C, in the target's true covariate law
methods_compared: STC with the outcome model corrected
